title: Moving a device
summary: A device belongs to one organization for its whole life. Moving it to another organization of the same billing account archives it in the source and creates a linked successor in the target; readings are never copied or re-stamped. The top row is the request, with the move in status stopping. The second row is the cutover, one transaction, after which the move is completed or failed.

boxes.label: Mover
boxes.detail: A member of the source and the target who holds Device.move in each. The billing account still grants nothing: the targets offered are the account's other organizations where this person holds the permission.

boxes.label: Review
boxes.detail: Changes nothing. For up to 100 devices it says how each reports, which profile versions are copied, what ends, the choice for each dashboard and automation that uses them, and what blocks the move: an archived device, one waiting for the runtime or already moving, a directly connected device, a code taken in the target. It also says when automations are turned off in the target. The review carries a hash.

boxes.label: Confirm
boxes.detail: Idempotent by operation_uuid. Under a lock on both organizations it checks the account and the permission again, rebuilds the review and compares its hash with the one the person saw; a difference answers 409 with the new review. Anything to be archived must be confirmed item by item.

boxes.label: Stop the active devices
boxes.detail: Each device with an applied configuration gets an ordinary deactivation, except that it keeps its place under the device limit. Its row in the move is stopping; a device that was not running is waiting. While a device is in a move it refuses other lifecycle and configuration requests.

boxes.label: Runtime
boxes.detail: To the runtime a move is a deactivation of one device and, later, an activation of another. It never changes a device's organization: stored rows keep the organization_uuid they were written with.

boxes.label: ContinueDeviceMove
boxes.detail: When the runtime reports a stop, the device's row becomes stopped, or failed if the runtime refused, and this job runs. It locks the move and does nothing until every device has answered.

boxes.label: Cutover
boxes.detail: Checks once more that both organizations share the account, the mover still holds Device.move in both, no predecessor runs again and no code was taken meanwhile. Then it does everything at once: archive, create, link, hand over the device-limit place, end the predecessors' open alerts and geofence assignments, and record the move in both organizations' activity.

boxes.label: Successor device
boxes.sub: New device in the target, linked
boxes.detail: The predecessor is archived as moved. The successor is a new device with a new UUID, built from the predecessor's last applied configuration rewritten onto a copy of its profile version in the target. It keeps the same source: the adapter or gateway stays with its owner and the successor reports through it as a hosted device.

boxes.label: History
boxes.sub: Read where it was recorded, not copied
boxes.detail: If the mover includes it, the successor reads everything its predecessor's history showed at the cutover, earlier moves included, each part under the organization that recorded it and that organization's retention. A device moved back always reads what it recorded in its own organization. Laravel decides each crossing and asks the runtime once per organization. A source can stop sharing on its link, which cuts everything that crossed it for every later device; sharing also stops when either organization leaves the account.

boxes.label: Dashboards, automations
boxes.detail: The mover chooses for each one that uses a moving device. One that uses only moving devices can move; a dashboard that also uses others can be copied. A moved dashboard keeps its row. A moved automation is recreated in the target and the source's is archived as moved; one kept in the source that still binds a moved device is turned off. Where automations are off in the target, nobody can change or turn on a moved automation until they are turned on, and a mover holding Workflow.activate there can choose to turn them on at cutover.

boxes.label: Runtime activation
boxes.detail: A device that was running is activated in the target when the mover holds Device.activate there; otherwise its draft waits for a member of the target. From then on the runtime stores the same source's readings under the target's organization_uuid. Readings that arrive between the stop and this start are stored for neither.

boxes.label: Failed
boxes.detail: The source ends as it started. Every device the move stopped is activated again with its last applied configuration, as a system action, in the place it never gave up. A stop the runtime answers late is resumed when the answer arrives.

steps.text: Someone with Device.move in both organizations picks devices and a target in the same billing account. The review says what will happen and changes nothing.
Confirming rebuilds the review under a lock on both organizations. If anything changed since the person read it, the answer is 409 and they review again.
The move is created as stopping. Each running device gets an ordinary deactivation that keeps its device-limit place.
The runtime stops each device like any other deactivation and reports back.
Each answer marks that device stopped and queues the job that takes the move on.
If the runtime refuses a stop, the move fails and every device it had stopped is started again.
Once every device has stopped, the cutover runs. If none was running, it ran straight away inside the confirmation.
The cutover checks the account, the mover's permission and the devices again. A failed check fails the move with nothing moved.
Each predecessor is archived as moved and a successor is created in the target, on a copy of its profile version, linked to it.

Dashboards and automations that used the devices are moved, copied, kept or archived as the mover chose. If automations are off in the target, a moved automation waits there until they are turned on, which the mover may do in the same move.
A device that was running starts again in the target. The same source now feeds a device of another organization, and new readings are stored for that organization.
Earlier readings stay where they were recorded. If the mover included them, the successor reads the whole history its predecessor had, through every earlier move, until a source stops sharing.
